analysis:
This batch contains documentation only: the new changelog, a hardware-support.md Context paragraph plus date bump, and the inference.md metadata unit. The inference.md patch excerpt in file_changes (head lines 25-171, 876-877) was not supplied as an input unit, so it was not fully reviewed. The docs describe a new unregistered Nemotron Super local text and image owner reachable through an opt-in HTTP hook, which is disabled by default. They describe three pieces of new surface.

First, a CPU PNG/JPEG decoder (ImageIO, EXIF/XMP orientation) processes consumer-supplied inline images. Geometry is said to be bounded before allocation, but this could not be verified. This relates to TB-007, the T-050 media-plaintext class and A-001.

Second, env-driven features: MTP speculation, concurrent decode (up to 8 requests), and a prefill chunk setting. The unverified part is whether the DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_* variables are operator-only.

Third, a RAM checkpoint prefix bank enabled by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY. This conflicts with the T-041 and hardware-support.md statements (lines 104-105 in the head file) that no RAM prefix-cache carve exists in production. I reported it as a low-severity threat-model gap.

The changelog says the HTTP hook uses existing auth and 429 busy handling, and that the load rechecks a pending LOAD lease. The code for these is not supplied. The next pass should check: tenant or salt scoping of the checkpoint bank, the auth path of the HTTP hook, decoder resource bounds, and whether the hook bypasses TB-002 E2E decryption or the TB-011 serving authorization. Because no source is available, none of this is confirmed safe.

findings.detail: The changelog adds `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse. It uses a resident recurrent checkpoint bank sized at min(1 GiB, grant/8) and reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and hardware-support.md state that production never constructs a resident-RAM prefix cache, that ramPrefix is always 0, and that SSD is the sole tier. The changelog does not say that cross-account scoping (coordinator-authored cacheSalt) or the SEC-035 TTFT-oracle sign-off applies to this bank. It does say client prompt-cache keys are rejected, which leaves it unclear what scopes reuse. If the hook is served to multiple tenants, one account can detect another's prefix by hit/miss latency. The current text also gives no TTL or purge for the bank. The code is not in this batch, so this is a threat-model gap rather than a confirmed bug. Fix: add the RAM tier and its scoping, TTL and kill-switch semantics to T-041, or state that the hook is single-tenant/local only. Make the bank require an authenticated per-account salt before it can be enabled for coordinator traffic.
findings.title: Opt-in resident-RAM prefix checkpoint bank contradicts T-041's 'no production RAM tier' posture
